summary: This is a project specification for DocuVerse, a containerized Markdown documentation server. It describes a four-service architecture with a Python FastAPI backend that serves Markdown files with caching and search, a Next.js React frontend that displays them beautifully, and Redis and Meilisearch services for performance and searching. The entire system runs in Docker containers orchestrated together.

explanations.18: The backend will use markdown-it-py to convert Markdown text into HTML, with extra plugins added to make code blocks pretty (syntax highlighting) and create clickable anchor links for headings.
explanations.23: A SHA256 hash is a unique fingerprint of the file's content—if the same Markdown file is requested twice, its hash will be identical, letting us recognize we've already processed it.
explanations.24: Redis is being used as a key-value store where we save the HTML output using the hash as the lookup key, so we don't have to convert the same Markdown to HTML repeatedly.
explanations.28: On startup, the backend scans the entire `/docs` folder recursively to find every `.md` file, converts it to plain text, and uploads it to Meilisearch so users can search across all documentation.
explanations.31: This endpoint returns a nested JSON structure that mirrors the folder and file organization on disk, like how a file explorer shows folders containing files and subfolders.
explanations.34: Beyond just the rendered HTML, this endpoint also returns a table of contents—a structured list of all the headings in the document with their hierarchy levels so the UI can display them in a sidebar.
explanations.39: The backend needs an endpoint to serve images and other non-Markdown files that the documentation might reference, similar to how a web server serves static assets.
explanations.48: As the user scrolls through the main content, the Table of Contents sidebar on the right should visually highlight which section they're currently reading.
explanations.53: The dark/light mode toggle should automatically match what the user's operating system is set to (light or dark mode), but users can override it manually.
explanations.58: The print stylesheet ensures that when someone prints the documentation, only the main content appears in a nicely formatted way without the distracting sidebars and navigation.
explanations.64: A multi-stage build means the Docker image is constructed in multiple steps—first compiling/installing everything, then copying only the final artifacts into a smaller production image to save space.
explanations.70: The documentation folder is mounted as read-only (`:ro`) so the running application cannot accidentally modify the user's original Markdown files.
